M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; density standard reference. Dissolution enthalpy +35.4 kJ/mol derived from NBS/Wagman 1982 formation enthalpies: Pb(NO3)2(s) -451.9, Pb2+(aq) -1.7, NO3-(aq) -207.4 kJ/mol, so -1.7 + 2(-207.4) + 451.9 = +35.4. Calorimetric values around +33.6 are also quoted; the 2 kJ/mol spread is the disagreement between the two routes and is not resolved here. Cp(s) 145 is an ESTIMATE from the nitrates' range, not a sourced value, and nothing computed depends on it while the salt is dissolved

Kerotakis household-material assumptions v1: explicit unbranded teaching surrogates for common household substances; ACS middle-school chemistry uses 3% peroxide for yeast catalysis, documents detergent-lowered surface tension, teaches that vegetable oil is less dense than water and does not dissolve in it, demonstrates that detergent helps oil and water mix, and its Colors on the Move activity records detergent driving food colouring rapidly across whole milk; a Journal of Chemical Education baker's-yeast gasometer study measures CO2 evolution, induction, steady production and nutrient depletion, while FAO fermentation material gives the balanced hexose-to-ethanol-and-CO2 pathway; American Society of Baking compressed-yeast technical guidance reports 70% moisture and 30% solids; USDA ERS reports cow's milk as approximately 87% water with the balance milk fat and skim solids; ACS Making Glue and Mississippi State Extension describe vinegar separating milk casein into heavy white curds and liquid whey
